title: Why can the angle APB not be named as just the angle P?
description: Three rays start at the point P. Taking the rays two at a time gives more than one angle at P, so the letter P alone does not say which angle is meant. A point on each arm is needed in the name.
teaching_notes: One idea: when more than one angle shares a vertex, the vertex letter alone is not enough, and the name needs a point on each arm. Watch for students who think the vertex letter is always enough.

source: Explain why angle APB cannot be labelled as angle P.
video_script.why: The child counts the angles that share the vertex P and sees that the letter P alone cannot tell them apart.
video_script.substitution: Take the three rays at P two at a time, and list the angles they make.

final_answer.value: Three angles share the vertex P: angle APB, angle BPC and angle APC. The name angle P does not say which one is meant, so we name a point on each arm
final_answer.spoken: three angles share the vertex P. They are eigh P B, B P C and eigh P C. The name P alone does not say which angle is meant, so we name a point on each arm

never_show: the count of the angles at P, before the answer beat
maths_rules: At P there are three rays, PA, PB and PC, and all of them start at P.
Any two of these rays make an angle with the vertex P.
The pairs are PA and PB, PB and PC, and PA and PC, so there are three angles at P.
The name P alone is the same for all three, so it does not say which angle is meant.
A name with a point on each arm, such as APB, shows which two arms are used.
video_script.design: One idea: when several angles share a vertex, the name needs a point on each arm. The figure stays on the board and each pair of rays lights up in turn. The method is the same way as the examples in the book on the arms and the vertex of an angle.
